content.text: The document expressly disclaims any minimum commitment.

input.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
input.rationale: Clause 2.1 meets the preferred position outright: there is no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, Customer pays only for Services actually ordered under an executed Order Form, and declining to place further orders is expressly not a breach or shortfall. This is reinforced by clause 7.1 (Vendor may not impose minimum-use or similar charges not identified in the Order Form) and clause 12.3 (Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment). Clause 8.2 allows Customer to opt out of any Order Form renewal on thirty days' notice, so no multi-year take-or-pay exposure arises, and the renewal uplift is capped under 8.3. The only "shortfall" concept in the document is the usage true-up in clause 22 audit rights, which is a true-up of undisputed under-reported quantities rather than a take-or-pay penalty. No volume caps on Customer usage were found. No redline required.
